cards.label: {today} — Whitechapel
cards.text: Rent's due Monday. You have £40, and this morning's interviewer has promised to keep your details on file. Archie, an old mate, said he might have work. So: Tuesday night, behind a chicken shop on Mile End Road.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: He's whistling, a Tesco bag hooked on one finger. "Two blokes, cash, in and out before the chicken shop shuts. You just stand there looking like you'd be a pain to fight. If I say leg it, you leg it. Don't wait for me."

cards.speaker: You
cards.text: "I don't look like I'd be a pain to fight."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Pretend you're Vinnie Jones in his prime, then." He looks you up and down. "Bit more of a Mr Bean vibe, but you make do with what you've got." He holds out a fist. "You in?"

choices.label: "I'll stand there."
choices.result_text: You bump the fist. "Lovely," says Archie, and goes back to whistling.

choices.label: "Who are the buyers?"
choices.result_text: Archie lowers the fist. "Two lads from Romford. Bought off me twice. Pay cash, don't chat." He thinks about it. "One of them's got a cousin. Never met the cousin."

choices.label: "I want half."
choices.result_text: "You were getting half." Archie looks at you for a long second, fist still out. "Sixty-forty, then. Your way. Don't make a habit of it."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: He pulls something from his coat and presses it into your hand: a small glass hourglass, warm. "One of James's. If it goes bad, break it." He doesn't say what it does. He's already watching the road.

choices.label: Take it
choices.result_text: You put it in your pocket, where it keeps being warm.

cards.text: The buyers arrive in a grey Vauxhall. Three of them, one more than Archie mentioned. He stops whistling.

cards.label: It goes wrong
cards.text: The third man gets out last, in no hurry. The other two straighten up. They call him Nick. He holds out a hand for the Tesco bag, looks in, and hands it back. "Light." Nobody has said a number. One of the others opens a Stanley knife.

cards.speaker: Nick
cards.text: He looks you over and takes his time about it. "New one. Lovely. Stay there, new one. You can watch." He's smiling before the sentence is finished.
Nick cracks his knuckles, one at a time. Archie edges half a step in front of you.

intro: Nick doesn't wait for anyone to be ready.

lessons.1: Archie's down. Nick's coming for you.
lessons.2: Read what he's about to do.
lessons.3: You can't win this. Look at the bar.

cards.text: The alley, a second earlier. You shout. Archie's forearms are up when Nick's fist arrives, and the punch goes nowhere useful. Something small breaks on the tarmac. Nick slows, mid-sneer. All three do, like a video buffering.

cards.label: Four streets later
cards.text: A closed launderette. Archie leans on the shutter, eyes streaming, the Tesco bag still hooked on his finger. "Pub," he says.
